Welcome

Hello, Fellow Dog Person.

Dogs are weird. Let's just say it out loud. They spin in circles before lying down. They bark at leaves. They act like they haven't eaten in years, eight minutes after breakfast. They steal socks, sneeze when they're excited and stare at us while we eat with the intensity of a courtroom drama.

And we love them. Absolutely, completely, ridiculously.

This book celebrates more than 100 real dog breeds, from tiny bosses to gentle giants, from fluffy legends to professional couch potatoes. Each profile mixes real facts about history, size, lifespan, grooming and training with a healthy dose of humor. Because every breed has a personality, and every personality has a story.

Read it cover to cover, open it anywhere or use it to settle family debates about which dog is the most dramatic. (Spoiler: it's the Husky.)

Grab a cozy blanket, a hot drink and preferably a dog. Let's meet the weirdos we love.

Woof, and happy reading!

9
The Drama Queens

Siberian Husky

Origin: Siberia (Russia)
No.001

Quick Stats

Height20–23.5 in
Weight35–60 lb
Lifespan12–14 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForMarathon runners, cold-climate homes and anyone who enjoys being argued with.
The Hilarious Truth

A Husky does not bark. A Husky files a formal verbal complaint, with a dramatic opening, a heartfelt middle and an encore nobody asked for. Ask it to sit and it will howl a three-act opera about the injustice of sitting.

Origin & History

Developed by the Chukchi people of northeastern Siberia as sled dogs that could pull light loads over huge distances in brutal cold. Brought to Alaska in 1908 for sled racing.

Personality & Temperament

Friendly, mischievous, independent and famously talkative. Loves people, loves running even more, and treats fences as a polite suggestion.

★ Surprising Fact

In 1925, relay teams of sled dogs, including Huskies like Balto and Togo, carried diphtheria serum nearly 700 miles to Nome, Alaska. The race inspired the Iditarod.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A theater major who escapes every party through the bathroom window, then posts a moody photo of a frozen lake.

Secret Superpower

Can open a 'Husky-proof' latch in under four minutes.

If It Could Talk

“AROOOO-woo-woo. Translation: I have been fed. But have I been fed emotionally?”

10
The Drama Queens

Pug

Origin: China
No.002

Quick Stats

Height10–13 in
Weight14–18 lb
Lifespan13–15 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForApartment dwellers, homebodies and fans of loud, heartfelt snoring.
The Hilarious Truth

The Pug's face is permanently set to 'Did you just say what I think you said?' It snores like a leaf blower, sneezes like a trumpet and believes every closed door is a personal betrayal.

Origin & History

One of the oldest breeds on earth, kept as cherished lap dogs by Chinese emperors over 2,000 years ago. Dutch traders brought them to Europe, where they became royal favorites.

Personality & Temperament

Charming, affectionate and comic. Pugs live to be near their people and are happiest when they are the center of attention, which is always.

★ Surprising Fact

A Pug named Pompey is credited with saving William the Silent, Prince of Orange, by barking to warn him of approaching assassins in 1572.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A beloved talk-show host who gasps at every audience question and somehow makes it charming.

Secret Superpower

Turns any frown upside down by simply existing in your field of vision.

If It Could Talk

“Excuse me. EXCUSE ME. Is that cheese? Why was I not informed about the cheese?”

11
The Drama Queens

Shih Tzu

Origin: Tibet / China
No.003

Quick Stats

Height9–10.5 in
Weight9–16 lb
Lifespan10–18 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForFamilies who love grooming days and anyone needing a full-time cuddle consultant.
The Hilarious Truth

The Shih Tzu wakes up gorgeous, demands a blowout anyway, and expects room service by 9 a.m. Its hair has its own scheduling assistant.

Origin & History

Bred from Tibetan dogs gifted to Chinese royalty, the Shih Tzu ('little lion') was a prized palace companion of the Ming and Qing dynasties for centuries.

Personality & Temperament

Affectionate, outgoing and happy to spend the day on your lap. Not built for work, built for adoration.

★ Surprising Fact

The breed nearly vanished after the fall of the Chinese imperial court; modern Shih Tzus descend from just 14 dogs, including seven males and seven females.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A celebrity who travels with a ring light and a personal humidifier, but is genuinely very nice to the waiters.

Secret Superpower

Can turn a single sigh into a guilt trip lasting 45 minutes.

If It Could Talk

“Do not touch my topknot. I have a look going.”

12
The Drama Queens

Basset Hound

Origin: France
No.004

Quick Stats

HeightUp to 15 in
Weight40–65 lb
Lifespan12–13 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForRelaxed households, kids who like gentle friends and anyone who appreciates long ears.
The Hilarious Truth

Every Basset Hound sighs like a tired Victorian poet who has just been asked to help you move. Its ears drag through the water bowl, and it cannot believe you would let that happen.

Origin & History

Developed by French monks and aristocrats to trail rabbits on foot. 'Basset' comes from the French 'bas', meaning low.

Personality & Temperament

Gentle, patient and stubborn. Bassets are mellow at home but transform into determined detectives the moment they catch a scent.

★ Surprising Fact

A Basset's long ears sweep scent particles up toward its nose as it walks. Its nose holds well over 200 million scent receptors, second only to the Bloodhound.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A retired detective who solves your missing-sock case, then naps for nine hours.

Secret Superpower

Can locate a dropped potato chip from three rooms away while appearing to be asleep.

If It Could Talk

“Sigh. Fine. I will walk. But only to the corner, and I will be emotional about it.”

13
The Drama Queens

Cavalier King Charles Spaniel

Origin: United Kingdom
No.005

Quick Stats

Height12–13 in
Weight13–18 lb
Lifespan12–15 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForFirst-time owners, seniors, families and anyone who wants a velvet shadow.
The Hilarious Truth

The Cavalier gazes at you like you are the main character in a romantic period drama. You opened a granola bar. It has already composed a sonnet about your hands.

Origin & History

Descended from toy spaniels beloved by King Charles II, who reportedly was rarely seen without them. The modern Cavalier was re-created in the 1920s to match old paintings.

Personality & Temperament

Sweet, gentle, eager to please and wonderfully adaptable. Equally happy on a hike or on a velvet sofa.

★ Surprising Fact

Legend says King Charles II decreed that his spaniels be allowed in any public place, including Parliament. The story is popular, though no such law has ever been found.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A hopeless romantic who cries at every wedding, including strangers' weddings visible from a park bench.

Secret Superpower

Melts the hearts of even self-declared 'not a dog person' humans.

If It Could Talk

“Is it time for cuddles? I think it is time for cuddles. It is always time for cuddles.”

14
The Drama Queens

Maltese

Origin: Malta
No.006

Quick Stats

Height7–9 in
WeightUnder 7 lb
Lifespan12–15 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForApartment owners, fans of grooming and anyone who wants a glamorous travel buddy.
The Hilarious Truth

The Maltese is a cotton ball with opinions. It weighs less than a gallon of milk but walks into a room like it owns the building, the street and your weekend plans.

Origin & History

One of the oldest toy breeds, prized on the island of Malta for at least 2,000 years. Greeks and Romans adored them as companions.

Personality & Temperament

Gentle, playful and fearless. Maltese are lively little charmers who think every visitor came to see them specifically.

★ Surprising Fact

The Maltese has a single coat with no undercoat, so it sheds very little and its hair keeps growing much like human hair.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A tiny fashion editor who rejects your outfit with a single raised eyebrow.

Secret Superpower

Can look freshly groomed and deeply offended at the same time.

If It Could Talk

“Is that a puddle? I'm being carried, right? Right.”

15
The Drama Queens

Afghan Hound

Origin: Afghanistan
No.007

Quick Stats

Height25–27 in
Weight50–60 lb
Lifespan12–18 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForExperienced owners, people with secure fences and lovers of hair.
The Hilarious Truth

The Afghan Hound walks into a room like a rock star arriving at a 1970s photo shoot. Wind machine not included. It does not need one. The wind simply follows it.

Origin & History

An ancient sighthound from the mountains of Afghanistan, bred to chase gazelles and hares over rugged terrain. Its silky coat protected it from cold.

Personality & Temperament

Aloof, dignified and independent, with a silly, clownish side reserved for trusted people.

★ Surprising Fact

In 2005, an Afghan Hound named Snuppy became the world's first cloned dog, created by scientists in South Korea.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A supermodel who wears sunglasses indoors and only answers questions in single words.

Secret Superpower

Can sprint up to 40 mph while looking like a shampoo commercial.

If It Could Talk

“Darling. Darling. I don't do 'fetch.'”

16
The Drama Queens

Bichon Frise

Origin: Mediterranean / France
No.008

Quick Stats

Height9.5–11.5 in
Weight12–18 lb
Lifespan14–15 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForFamilies, allergy-conscious homes (low shedding) and cheerful people.
The Hilarious Truth

A Bichon Frise is a powder puff that got a scholarship to clown college. It will do one trick, bow, and wait for a standing ovation and a treat-shaped Oscar.

Origin & History

Descended from Mediterranean water spaniels, Bichons sailed with seafarers and later charmed French royalty. They also performed in circuses.

Personality & Temperament

Cheerful, curious and playful. Bichons love everyone and perform tricks for applause.

★ Surprising Fact

Bichons are known for the 'Bichon Blitz', explosive bursts of zoomies around the house that can last several minutes.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A cheerful birthday-party entertainer who never takes off the balloon hat, even at the grocery store.

Secret Superpower

Can turn a bad day into a good one in one hop.

If It Could Talk

“Ta-da! Did you see that? Do you want to see it again? I'm doing it again!”

17
The Drama Queens

Italian Greyhound

Origin: Italy
No.009

Quick Stats

Height13–15 in
Weight7–14 lb
Lifespan14–15 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForWarm homes, gentle households and people who love blankets.
The Hilarious Truth

The Italian Greyhound shivers at 71 degrees, wears a cashmere sweater and treats a light breeze as a weather emergency. It sleeps burrowed under three blankets like a burrito with legs.

Origin & History

A miniature sighthound treasured in Renaissance Italy and found in art from ancient Pompeii. Favored by royals including Catherine the Great.

Personality & Temperament

Sensitive, affectionate and playful. Loves warmth, blankets and its favorite person, in that order.

★ Surprising Fact

Italian Greyhounds have very little body fat and a thin coat, so many own sweaters for any temperature below 'perfect.'

If This Dog Were a Person…

A poet who drinks herbal tea, writes about the moon and gets cold in July.

Secret Superpower

Can locate the single warmest spot in any house within seconds.

If It Could Talk

“Is the heater on? It is not on enough.”

The Drama Queens

Papillon

Origin: France / Belgium
No.010

Quick Stats

Height8–11 in
Weight5–10 lb
Lifespan14–16 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForActive small-space dwellers and people interested in tricks or agility.
The Hilarious Truth

The Papillon looks like a delicate butterfly and has the personality of a fitness instructor who already did a 5K before you woke up. It learned 'sit' in four minutes and now wants a new curriculum.

Origin & History

A toy spaniel named for its butterfly-shaped ears ('papillon' is French for butterfly). Seen in paintings by Old Masters like Titian and Rubens.

Personality & Temperament

Alert, friendly and surprisingly athletic. A tiny dog with big brains and boundless enthusiasm.

★ Surprising Fact

Despite weighing under 10 pounds, Papillons regularly win agility and obedience competitions against much larger breeds.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A cheerful overachiever with three degrees and a color-coded planner.

Secret Superpower

Hears the treat bag open through two closed doors.

If It Could Talk

“I learned a new trick while you were in the shower. Want to see?”

19
The Drama Queens

Bloodhound

Origin: Belgium / France
No.011

Quick Stats

Height23–27 in
Weight80–110 lb
Lifespan10–12 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForRural homes, scent-sport fans and people with towels for drool.
The Hilarious Truth

The Bloodhound is a sad-faced detective who drools like a leaking faucet and finds your missing car keys, your teenager and that sandwich you hid last Tuesday.

Origin & History

Bred in medieval monasteries, notably the Abbey of Saint-Hubert, to track deer and boar. Their scent-trailing ability is legendary.

Personality & Temperament

Gentle, patient and endlessly determined once on a trail. Friendly at home, unstoppable outdoors.

★ Surprising Fact

Bloodhound tracking evidence has been accepted in U.S. courts. Their wrinkles and long ears help trap and funnel scent toward the nose.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A soft-spoken forensic expert who solves the case, then cries during the closing speech.

Secret Superpower

Can follow a trail several days old.

If It Could Talk

“I smell... a mystery. And also bacon. Mostly bacon.”

20
The Drama Queens

Poodle

Origin: Germany / France
No.012

Quick Stats

HeightOver 15 in (Standard)
Weight40–70 lb (Standard)
Lifespan10–18 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForActive families, allergy-conscious homes and anyone who loves a clever companion.
The Hilarious Truth

The Poodle has a genius-level IQ, a fancy hairdo and absolutely no patience for your nonsense. It knows you said 'walk' even when you spell it. It also knows you cannot afford that haircut.

Origin & History

Originally a German water retriever (the name comes from 'Pudel', to splash). The famous show clip once protected joints while swimming. France made it a national icon.

Personality & Temperament

Exceptionally smart, athletic, proud and people-oriented. Comes in Standard, Miniature and Toy sizes.

★ Surprising Fact

Poodles consistently rank among the most intelligent dog breeds and were once used as circus performers and truffle hunters.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A brilliant surgeon who also competes in ballroom dancing on weekends and makes it look easy.

Secret Superpower

Can solve a puzzle toy faster than you can read the instructions.

If It Could Talk

“I'm not high-maintenance. I'm high-quality.”

The Tiny Bosses

Chihuahua

Origin: Mexico
No.013

Quick Stats

Height5–8 in
WeightUp to 6 lb
Lifespan14–16 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForSingles, apartments and people who want a loyal pocket-sized protector.
The Hilarious Truth

The Chihuahua weighs four pounds and is ready to fight a bear, a mailman, or a leaf. It trembles not from fear but from sheer volume of opinions it has not yet expressed.

Origin & History

Named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua, the breed likely descends from the Techichi, a companion dog of ancient Toltec and Aztec cultures.

Personality & Temperament

Bold, loyal and confident, with a strong bond to one person. A big personality in the world's smallest recognized breed.

★ Surprising Fact

The Chihuahua is the smallest dog breed recognized by the AKC. One Chihuahua, Miracle Milly, was recognized as the world's smallest living dog at about 3.8 inches tall.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A tiny bodyguard who wears sunglasses, has a walkie-talkie and takes the job extremely seriously.

Secret Superpower

Fits in a handbag; commands the entire house.

If It Could Talk

“Say that again. SAY IT AGAIN. I dare you.”

26
The Tiny Bosses

French Bulldog

Origin: France / England
No.014

Quick Stats

Height11–13 in
WeightUnder 28 lb
Lifespan10–12 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForCity living, busy professionals and anyone who enjoys grumbling with love.
The Hilarious Truth

The Frenchie is a tiny, grumpy CEO who wants the quarterly reports on its desk by noon. It snorts at your proposal, rejects your snack offering, then falls asleep on the keyboard.

Origin & History

Toy bulldogs from England traveled with lace workers to France in the 1800s, where they became Parisian café darlings with bat-like ears.

Personality & Temperament

Playful, adaptable and affectionate, with a stubborn streak. Frenchies are clowns who rarely bark but always comment.

★ Surprising Fact

The French Bulldog became the most popular dog breed in the U.S. in 2022, ending the Labrador Retriever's 31-year reign at the top of the AKC rankings.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A start-up founder in a black turtleneck who says 'Let's circle back' and then naps through the meeting.

Secret Superpower

Can deliver a judgmental stare that ends conversations.

If It Could Talk

“Your meeting has been canceled. I have scheduled a nap.”

27
The Tiny Bosses

Yorkshire Terrier

Origin: England
No.015

Quick Stats

Height7–8 in
WeightAround 7 lb
Lifespan11–15 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForCity life, small homes and owners who want a big-hearted travel pal.
The Hilarious Truth

The Yorkie is a former mill-rat hunter who now lives the luxury life, but has not forgotten the streets. Silk hair, steel spirit, absolutely zero chill.

Origin & History

Developed in Yorkshire during the Industrial Revolution to catch rats in textile mills and mines, then became a fashionable Victorian lap dog.

Personality & Temperament

Feisty, brave and affectionate. A terrier through and through, just in a silky, travel-size package.

★ Surprising Fact

A Yorkie named Smoky served with American soldiers in World War II and is often called one of the first therapy dogs. She also helped run telegraph wire through a narrow pipe.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A tiny rock star with perfect hair who still remembers playing grimy bars.

Secret Superpower

Detects an approaching delivery driver from half a mile away.

If It Could Talk

“Everyone stay calm. I will handle the doorbell.”

The Tiny Bosses

Dachshund

Origin: Germany
No.016

Quick Stats

Height8–9 in (Standard)
Weight16–32 lb (Standard)
Lifespan12–16 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForOwners who can protect backs (avoid stairs), apartment life and humor lovers.
The Hilarious Truth

The Dachshund is a sausage with the confidence of a lion. It's long, low and loud, with a bark designed for a dog four times its size. It will bury itself in your blankets and refuse to come out until you apologize.

Origin & History

German for 'badger dog,' the Dachshund was bred to dig into badger dens. Its long body and short legs were built for tunnels.

Personality & Temperament

Clever, courageous and stubborn, with a loud bark for its size. Comes in smooth, wire and long-haired coats.

★ Surprising Fact

A Dachshund named Waldi was the first official mascot of the Olympic Games, at the 1972 Munich Olympics.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A tiny, fearless lawyer who has never lost an argument and never once backed down.

Secret Superpower

Can fit into any blanket, tunnel or sleeping bag known to science.

If It Could Talk

“I am small in height but enormous in spirit. Also, I want your sandwich.”

29
The Tiny Bosses

Miniature Pinscher

Origin: Germany
No.017

Quick Stats

Height10–12.5 in
Weight8–10 lb
Lifespan12–16 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForActive owners who enjoy personality and have escape-proof fences.
The Hilarious Truth

The Min Pin trots through life like a parade horse on its way to accept a medal. It is ten pounds of espresso and ambition, and it will absolutely escape if given a two-inch gap.

Origin & History

Not a mini Doberman! The Min Pin is an older German breed developed to hunt rats in barns and stables.

Personality & Temperament

Fearless, energetic and proud. The self-proclaimed 'King of Toys' moves with a high-stepping prance.

★ Surprising Fact

The Miniature Pinscher's distinctive 'hackney gait' resembles the high-stepping trot of a show horse.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A motivational speaker who drinks four espressos, then gives a TED talk on productivity.

Secret Superpower

Escapes from a fenced yard with Hollywood heist skill.

If It Could Talk

“I am the King of Toys. Bow, peasants.”

Jack Russell Terrier

Origin: England
No.018

Quick Stats

Height10–15 in
Weight13–17 lb
Lifespan13–16 years
Grooming
Exercise
Trainability
Perfect ForVery active households, experienced owners and fans of nonstop entertainment.
The Hilarious Truth

The Jack Russell has two speeds: 'rocket launch' and 'asleep.' It springs off furniture like a pogo stick and treats every squirrel as a mortal enemy.

Origin & History

Developed by Reverend John 'Jack' Russell in 19th-century England to bolt foxes from their dens during hunts.

Personality & Temperament

Energetic, clever, fearless and tireless. Jack Russells need a job, or they will invent one, probably involving your garden.

★ Surprising Fact

Jack Russells can jump five times their height. One famous Jack Russell, Eddie, starred on the TV sitcom Frasier.

If This Dog Were a Person…

An extreme-sports athlete who skydives on weekends and drinks energy drinks for breakfast.

Secret Superpower

Can jump onto a kitchen counter from a standing start.

If It Could Talk

“Is that a squirrel? Is that a squirrel? IS THAT A—”

Relatable Content

Things Only Dog Owners Understand

Check off every one that's true. If you get all of them, congratulations: you're officially one of us.

  • You spell W-A-L-K out loud, and your dog still knows.
  • You have said 'Who's a good boy?' to a dog who just ate a couch cushion.
  • You own more toys for your dog than for any human in your family.
  • You narrate your dog's thoughts out loud in a special voice. Everyone does a different voice.
  • Your bed is technically king-size. You sleep on eight inches of it.
  • You have apologized to your dog for stepping on its tail. It was your fault. Somehow.
  • You have more photos of your dog on your phone than of yourself.
  • Lint rollers are a food group.
  • You cannot eat cheese in private. Ever.
  • You've canceled plans because your dog 'looked sad.'
  • You know every dog in the neighborhood by name, but none of the humans.
  • You check the weather for walk times, not for your outfit.
  • You have said 'Drop it' at least 400 times this year.
  • You come home and the first thing you say is a greeting to the dog.
  • Your car has a permanent nose-print art installation on the back window.
  • You speak fluent tail-wag.
  • You sit on the floor even though you own perfectly good furniture.
  • Your dog's birthday party had better attendance than yours.
54
Pure Joy

The Most Ridiculously Adorable Dog Personalities

Every dog has a personality type. Which one lives at your house?

The Velcro Buddy

Follows you into the bathroom. Every. Single. Time. (Vizsla, Havanese)

The Sock Thief

Collects one sock from every pair. Hoards them like treasure. (Labrador, Beagle)

The Gentle Leaner

Leans its entire 120-pound body against you as a hug. (Great Dane, Bernese)

The Sneeze-Greeter

Sneezes with excitement when you come home. (Pug, Boston Terrier)

The Toy Collector

Keeps every toy since puppyhood in a secret stash. (Golden Retriever)

The Window Watcher

Supervises the street like a nosy neighbor. (Tibetan Spaniel, Lhasa Apso)

The Talker

Woo-woos, grumbles and responds to every question. (Husky, Malamute)

The Snuggle Burrito

Cannot sleep unless fully wrapped in a blanket. (Italian Greyhound, Dachshund)

The Smiler

Grins at strangers and wins hearts. (Samoyed, Keeshond)

The Happy Dancer

Spins, wiggles and bounces with joy. (Boxer, Bichon Frise, Japanese Chin)

A Day in the Life

Dogs and Their Ridiculous Daily Habits

A typical day, minute by ridiculous minute.

  • 5:58 a.m.Stares at your face from two inches away until you wake up.
  • 6:15 a.m.Breakfast. Inhaled in 8 seconds. Looks shocked the bowl is empty.
  • 7:00 a.m.Morning walk. Sniffs one fire hydrant for 11 minutes.
  • 8:30 a.m.Escorts you to the door. Acts like you're leaving for war.
  • 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.Naps in 14 different locations. Barks at the mail carrier twice.
  • 4:45 p.m.Greets you like you've been gone for 37 years.
  • 5:30 p.m.Dinner begging rehearsal. Chooses the 'abandoned orphan' face.
  • 7:00 p.m.Zoomies! Runs laps for no reason. Crashes into the ottoman.
  • 9:30 p.m.Bed. Spins in three circles. Lies down on your side.
  • 2:13 a.m.Licks paw loudly. Very loudly. For 20 minutes.
70
The Science (Sort Of)

Why Do Dogs Do That?

Some of the weirdest habits actually have real explanations.

Spinning before lying down

An ancient instinct from wild ancestors who trampled grass into a cozy bed. Your memory foam mattress doesn't need trampling. Your dog disagrees.

Kicking grass after a potty break

Scent glands in the paws leave a 'This was me' message for the neighborhood.

Bringing you a shoe

A gift! An offering! Also, maybe a plea for attention.

Head tilting

Dogs may tilt their heads to hear better or see your face around their muzzles. It also works on humans like a cheat code.

Survival Guide

Which Dog Would Survive a Zombie Apocalypse?

Our experts ran the simulations. The results are… concerning.

Will Definitely Survive

Belgian MalinoisAlready trained for special operations. Probably leading the resistance.
Australian Cattle DogTireless, clever and capable of herding zombies into a corral.
Border CollieHas a plan. Has a backup plan. Has a spreadsheet.
Tibetan MastiffZombies take one look and walk the other way.
BasenjiSilent (no barking) and too independent to follow anyone into a trap.

Fifty-Fifty

BeagleWill survive as long as there's food. Will follow a zombie holding a sandwich.
Siberian HuskyEscapes everything, including danger. Also, howls at the worst moment.
ChihuahuaWill fight every zombie personally, outweighed 40 to one.

First to Go (Bless Them)

Golden RetrieverRuns to greet the first zombie. 'HI! NEW FRIEND!'
BulldogRefuses to run. Asks the zombies to come back after nap time.
PugGasps. Freezes. Gasps again.
GreyhoundFast enough to escape but too busy sleeping upside down to notice.

Independent, affectionate, intelligent and dignified.

★ Surprising Fact

The Dandie Dinmont is the only dog breed named after a fictional character.

If This Dog Were a Person…

A scholarly poet who wears tweed and sips tea at the library.

Secret Superpower

Can make a dramatic entrance with its 'topknot' hairdo.

If It Could Talk

“I am the hero of my own novel.”

119
Warning Signs

10 Signs Your Dog Is Manipulating You

You're not being paranoid. You're being played. Lovingly.

1

The Head Tilt

Deployed precisely when you're about to say 'no.' Success rate: 94 percent.

2

The Sad Eyes at Dinner

It has eaten. It has eaten twice. It is still 'starving.'

3

The Sudden Limp

Appears when it's time for a bath. Disappears when the treat bag opens.

4

The Gentle Paw

One paw on your knee. Then another. Then you're sharing your sandwich.

5

The Leash Delivery

Brings you the leash and drops it on your laptop. Message received.

6

The Fake Yawn

Pretends to be bored so you'll feel guilty and play.

7

The Bed Takeover

Starts at the foot of the bed. Ends on your pillow. Nobody knows how.

8

The Sigh

A long, theatrical sigh when you're working. Translation: 'You've abandoned me.'

9

The Butt Wiggle

When it knows it's in trouble, it wiggles. You forgive it. Every time.

10

The Look-Away

Caught with a sock? Avoids eye contact like a guilty teenager.

Score 8 or more? Your dog isn't manipulating you. Your dog is running a full-scale operation.

Pembroke Welsh Corgi

Origin: Wales
No.091

Quick Stats

Height10–12 in
WeightUp to 30 lb

Grooming

The Hilarious Truth

The Corgi is a tiny king with enormous confidence. It struts around on stubby legs like it owns the palace, the throne and your snack drawer.

Origin & History

A Welsh herding dog that nipped at the heels of cattle. Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 Corgis.

Personality & Temperament

Smart, affectionate, alert and playful. A big dog in a short body.

Can herd cattle with tiny legs.

The Ultimate Dog Personality Quiz

Which hilarious dog breed matches YOUR personality? Answer honestly, and keep track of your letters. No judgment. (Okay, a little judgment.)

1.It's Saturday morning. You...

  1. ARun 5 miles before breakfast.
  2. BStay in bed until noon, wrapped like a burrito.
  3. COrganize everyone else's plans.
  4. DMake a dramatic entrance to brunch.

2.Your ideal snack is...

  1. AA protein bar. Efficient.
  2. BWhatever's closest to the couch.
  3. CThe good snacks. The ones you hid from others.
  4. DSomething expensive, served on a tiny plate.

3.When someone disagrees with you, you...

  1. AChallenge them to a race.
  2. BTake a nap and forget about it.
  3. CExplain calmly why you are right, again.
  4. DSigh loudly and leave the room.

4.Your friends describe you as...

  1. AEnergetic and unstoppable.
  2. BChill, cozy and huggable.
  3. CA natural leader (bossy).
  4. DThe main character.

5.Your dream vacation is...

  1. AHiking the Rockies.
  2. BA hammock. Anywhere.
  3. CA place where you choose the restaurant.
  4. DParis. With photo shoots.

6.Your superpower would be...

  1. AInfinite stamina.
  2. BFalling asleep anywhere.
  3. CMind control.
  4. DMaking everyone stop and stare.

7.Pick a holiday tradition:

  1. AThe 5K Turkey Trot.
  2. BThe post-dinner nap.
  3. CRunning the gift exchange.
  4. DThe ugly-sweater fashion show.

8.Your motto is...

  1. ALet's GO!
  2. BFive more minutes.
  3. CMy house, my rules.
  4. DIt's not drama, it's art.

Count your letters, then turn the page!

Holiday Hazard Report

Dogs at Christmas: Who Would Destroy the Tree First?

Official odds of total tree destruction, calculated by our elves.

1

Labrador Retriever 95%

Tail-wagging alone will clear every ornament below 3 feet within 6 minutes.

2

Jack Russell Terrier 93%

Will scale the tree like Mount Everest to reach the shiny star.

3

Siberian Husky 90%

Steals the tree skirt, wears it, howls a holiday carol.

4

Beagle 88%

Finds every candy cane, cookie and chocolate ornament on the tree. (Keep chocolate away from dogs!)

5

Golden Retriever 84%

Gently removes every ornament, one by one, and brings it to you as a gift.

6

Dachshund 70%

Tunnels into the pile of presents. Emerges wearing a bow.

7

Bulldog 12%

Too busy napping under the tree. Mistaken for a present twice.

8

Greyhound 5%

Asleep. Wakes up in January.

Safety Note From the Elves

Keep chocolate, xylitol, grapes, raisins, tinsel, ribbon, and electrical cords out of paws' reach. Secure the tree to the wall, and choose shatterproof ornaments for the low branches.

Until Next Time

Dogs Are Weird.
We Love Them.

Thank you for spending time with the weirdest, sweetest, most lovable creatures on the planet.

Whether your dog is a drama queen, a tiny boss, a couch potato or a fluffy legend, one thing is true: life is better with a dog in it.

So go give your dog a hug, an extra treat or a belly rub. They've earned it. (And you know they'll pretend they haven't eaten in days.)

Merry Christmas, Happy Holidays and a wonderfully weird New Year from all of us, and from every dog in this book.

Merry Christmas! Woof!
